data.narrative:
Stratek Global is a growth-stage nuclear energy company founded by Kelvin Kemm. The valuation universe comprises 11 peers across the nuclear energy sector: 3 public companies (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private firms including Helion, Oklo, Valar Atomics, X-Energy, and Nano Nuclear Energy.

Peer-median valuation methodology was not applicable in this case. The nuclear energy sector contains only 6 same-sector comparable companies overall, and filtering by stage alignment (same-stage or adjacent-stage) and valuation tier yielded fewer than the required 3 datapoints to establish a reliable median. Applying an all-sector median would introduce material distortion risk given the sector's narrow representation and heterogeneous business models across modular, advanced, and fusion-focused approaches.

Without sufficient narrow-peer clustering, traditional comparable company analysis cannot be responsibly executed. A defensible valuation of Stratek Global would require alternative or supplementary methods—such as discounted cash flow analysis tied to project milestones, revenue multiple analysis if revenue data exists, or venture capital method benchmarking against deployed capital and expected exit multiples in nuclear energy. The primary uncertainty is the structural thinness of the comparable set; valuation credibility depends on whether management can anchor to operational metrics (MW capacity, deployment timelines, customer contracts) rather than peer trading multiples.
